data.title: Micron Stocks Slip 1.4% as Record Revenue Meets Cycle Doubts
data.description:
Micron Technology , the AI-memory and storage-chip producer, reported record fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $54.23 billion, yet shares fell approximately 1.4% to $1,082 at 11.50am on Friday, Oct. 2. The valuation picture adds a wrinkle: that price sits 46.69% above the $737.60 GF Value estimate, leaving less room for disappointment than a low earnings multiple might suggest.

The cash engine is running hard. Quarterly operating cash flow reached $43.97 billion as revenue jumped 379% from a year earlier. According to Barron's reporting, data-center customers accounted for 63% of quarterly sales, while the stock traded at roughly 6.4 times projected fiscal-year earnings. Management expects memory supply to remain tight through 2028. Those earnings expectations explain how Micron can look inexpensive on one valuation measure and stretched on another.

The real test comes when supply catches up. Micron's strategic customer agreements give management greater confidence in future financial performance, but contracts cannot erase the risk of excess capacity or weaker pricing. Investors need evidence that today's cash surge can survive a softer memory market. Huge profits grab attention. Durable profits earn a higher multiple.

data.title: Why Medtronic's $4 Billion MiniMed Exchange Offer Is Losing Its Allure — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Bary

Medtronic's $4 billion exchange offer for its shares of MiniMed Group is a lot less attractive now that MiniMed's stock has dropped since the offer was unveiled a couple of weeks ago.

That could reduce participation and possibly prompt Medtronic to sweeten the deal. The tax-free exchange offer allows Medtronic investors to swap their shares for MiniMed shares held by Medtronic in what Wall Street calls a split-off.

Medtronic didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The big medical device maker owns 90% of MiniMed, which manufactures diabetes treatment products.

Medtronic took MiniMed public earlier this year; rather than spin off that remaining stake, Medtronic is offering its investors the exchange offer in what amounts to a stock buyback financed with MiniMed stock.

Medtronic is offering to swap some 225 million MiniMed shares-80% of its stake-for Medtronic stock with the option to swap its entire 90% stake, depending on demand.

The inducement: Medtronic holders would get MiniMed stock at a 7% discount to its market price. A discount in the 7%-to-10% range is common in split-off exchange offers such as Johnson & Johnson's exchange offer for Kenvue stock in 2023.

The problem for Medtronic is that MiniMed stock has dropped since the deal was announced on Sept. 14 and the discount is now just 3%, Barron's estimates.

MiniMed shares, which were trading Friday at $19.68, are down about 12% from $22.50 on Sept. 11, the trading day before the exchange offer was made. Medtronic stock, at $87.86, is off about 3%.

The drop in MiniMed could partly reflect selling by arbitragers.

Medtronic holders have until Oct. 9 to decide whether to participate, based on Barron's interpretation of the exchange offer document.

Medtronic is capping the number of MiniMed stock at 4.5939 shares for each Medtronic share. With the drop in MiniMed stock, investors stand to get the capped amount, which represents a roughly 3% discount-not the original 7%, Barron's estimates.

The final ratio is being calculated based on the price of the two stocks next week. A running total of the ratio and other information is available online.

With the discount now just 3%, it's possible that Medtronic could up the offer and extend the deadline.

One group of investors stands to benefit from the exchange offer. Holders of fewer than 100 shares of Medtronic who submit all their stock benefit from a so-called odd-lot provision that allows them to fully exchange all their stock.

Other Medtronic holders are subject to proration: They could get only a fraction of their shares exchanged if demand is high, which is often the case with exchange offers.

The odd-lot provision, which is common, has benefited small investors in other deals such as the 2024 offer by Cummins for its stake in Atmus Filtration Technologies. Atmus stock has doubled since then.

Medtronic and MiniMed have different investor bases.

Medtronic is a leading medical-device manufacturer that trades for about 15 times earnings and has a $110 billion market value, while MiniMed is much smaller at $5 billion and has stronger growth prospects from such products as insulin pumps for diabetics. It trades for about 30 times forward earnings.

The most comparable company to MiniMed is Dexcom, a much larger company in the diabetes market.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com

data.title: LPC, Electrical Equipment Distributor, Files for Nasdaq Capital Market IPO
data.description:
LPC, a Cayman holding company operating in Malaysia through its subsidiary Lotus Power Corporation (M) Sdn. Bhd., filed for an initial public offering on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "LPCI." The company plans to offer 3,750,000 ordinary shares at an expected price range of $4.00 to $6.00 per share. Prior to the IPO, there has been no public market for its shares.

Business Description

LPC is a Cayman Islands holding company that conducts operations in Malaysia through its subsidiary, Lotus Power Corporation (M) Sdn. Bhd. The company supplies medium- and high-voltage electrical distribution equipment—primarily switchgear and transformers—sourced from third-party OEMs. It provides integrated support for projects, including specification alignment, procurement coordination, technical compliance reviews, factory acceptance testing, logistics to site, and where required, coordination of installation, testing, and commissioning with manufacturers and third-party contractors.

LPC’s core product lines include medium-voltage switchgear and transformers, extra-high-voltage switchgear, power transformers, and low-voltage feeder pillars, serving buildings and infrastructure, utilities, industrial plants, railways and substations, renewable energy, mining, marine and offshore, and data centers. Competitive strengths include decades-long industry experience, established relationships with a leading Malaysian switchgear producer and a German-headquartered transformer manufacturer, commercial flexibility, and project coordination capabilities. The company plans to use IPO proceeds to expand into local assembly, develop proprietary products, and move into 132/275 kV supply, while strengthening tendering and execution capacity.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Asia-Pacific electric power T&D equipment market was ~$111.3B in 2022, projected to reach ~$190.8B by 2030.
  • Market growth: Asia-Pacific T&D equipment market CAGR ~7.0% (2023–2030); Southeast Asia T&D market CAGR ~5.3% (2024–2033).
  • Market position: LPC acts as a solutions provider and distributor in Malaysia’s medium- and high-voltage space with established OEM relationships.
  • Key competitors: Global OEMs and regional producers of switchgear/transformers; local distributors and EPC-oriented providers.
  • Industry trends: Grid modernization, renewable integration, rising data-center demand, and utility-led network investments in Malaysia (e.g., TNB’s RM90B grid plan).

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Served approximately 196 unique customers in FY 2026 across Malaysia.
  • Locations: Principal office at Subang Jaya, Selangor, Malaysia; owns and leases multiple properties used for office, storage, and rental.
  • Geographic presence: Operates across East and West Malaysia.
  • Partnerships: Established sourcing relationships with a Malaysian switchgear manufacturer and a German-headquartered transformer manufacturer.
  • Supplier concentration: Top two suppliers represented ~84.3% of purchases in FY 2026 (91.2% for top five).
  • Project support: Coordinates factory acceptance tests, on-site delivery, and, when required, installation/testing/commissioning with OEMs and contractors.

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): $23.0 million (FY 2026)
  • Revenue growth: Down 3.9% year over year (FY 2026 vs. FY 2025)
  • Gross profit: $3.43 million (14.9% margin)
  • Operating income: $1.52 million
  • Net income: $1.14 million

Management

  • Ong Chuan Lam, Chief Executive Officer; Executive Director; Chairman - Over 40 years in electrical engineering and power distribution; led Lotus Power since 1995; holds B.E.E. (West Virginia Institute of Technology) and MBA (University of Hull).
  • Ho Pui Lung, Executive Director - More than 25 years in building services and energy management; leadership roles at Wang & Lee; registered engineer and energy assessor.
  • Lai Kian Huat, Chief Financial Officer - 30+ years in accounting, audit, taxation, corporate finance; former executive director at Ni Hsin Group Berhad; served as independent director at a Nasdaq-listed company.
  • Rafchiek Joseph Michael, Independent Director Nominee - Three decades in manufacturing engineering and program startup, including roles at Boeing.
  • Teh Seng Pin, Independent Director Nominee - 15+ years in IPO readiness and capital markets advisory across Malaysia, Singapore, and Hong Kong.
  • Tong Ka Wai, Independent Director Nominee - Seasoned accounting and audit professional; partner at Nexus CPA Limited; experience as CFO and financial controller.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: LPC Limited
  • Filing date: October 02, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: LPCI
  • Exchange: Nasdaq Capital Market
  • Price range: $4.00 – $6.00
  • Offering size: Approximately $18.75 million at midpoint (excl. over-allotment)
  • Shares offered: 3,750,000 Ordinary Shares (plus 562,500 over-allotment option)
  • Lead underwriters: Sutter Securities, Inc.; Boustead Securities, LLC
  • Use of proceeds: ~60% to expand manufacturing/assembly and product range (including 132/275 kV), ~20% to strengthen project execution and sales (bonds, guarantees, strategic inventory, hiring), and ~20% for general working capital and public company costs.

Original SEC Filing: LPC LTD - F-1 - Oct. 02, 2026

data.title: CBOT wheat ends nearly unchanged, hovering near six-week lows
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures ended nearly unchanged on Friday, hovering near six-week lows, as a Saudi Arabian import tender boosted demand sentiment even as strength in the US dollar continued to cap prices, market analysts said.

  • CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) closed 1/4-cent higher at $6.83 per bushel.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) ended down 2-1/4 cents at $7.35-1/4 a bushel, and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) settled up 1-1/4 cents at $6.98 a bushel.

  • Saudi Arabia announced on Thursday that it was seeking to buy 535,000 metric tons of wheat for shipment in November and December. Traders viewed the tender as a sign that the recent price fall was stirring fresh demand after Saudi Arabia canceled its previous wheat tender on September 7 because of high prices.

  • The dollar index was on track for a fourth straight weekly gain against the euro on Friday, supported by elevated US Treasury yields amid a selloff in European government bond markets and expectations the Federal Reserve will maintain its hawkish interest rate stance. US currency strength makes dollar-denominated commodities more expensive for overseas buyers.

  • A lack of progress in diplomatic efforts to restore normal shipping through the Black Sea also underpinned wheat prices. Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday rejected proposals for a truce in Black Sea attacks.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Selloff Resumes After Brief Respite — 4th Update
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru and Paulo Trevisani

Treasury yields hovered near multidecade highs Friday as investors looked past slower-than-expected job creation in the U.S. amid lingering concerns about the long-term economic outlook.

The Labor Department said a net 29,000 jobs were created in September, well below the 84,000 expected in a Wall Street Journal consensus. Past figures were revised downward by a total of 60,000 over August and July. The unemployment rate ticked higher to 4.2% from 4.1%.

The 10-year yield slipped on the morning data to an intraday low of 5.155%, before snapping back to 5.285%, close to 2007 highs reached earlier this week.

While Friday's labor numbers alleviated pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates for a second consecutive meeting when it convenes late this month, they didn't squelch all fears. Oil prices walked back early losses and Brent turned slightly higher, keeping inflation concerns alive.

The rise in yields is also driven by concerns about fast-rising borrowing by large AI corporations and ballooning government debt.

"Practically, this is a fiscal responsibility story," F/m Investments CEO Alex Morris said. "We have exactly zero politicians running on fiscal responsibility [and] I think that is going to be the bigger problem."

Increasing government borrowing in Europe is helping push global yields up, Morris said.

"I don't think it's as pronounced as folks are saying, but I do think there's some crowding out effect that's injuring Treasury rates," he said.

The 10-year French benchmark yield reached a 24-year high while the comparable German government-bond yields dropped sharply, before recovering some ground, LSEG data showed.

The spread between French and German 10-year sovereign bond yields jumped to its most since November 2011, reaching 158.67 basis points, up from around 84 points in September. The widening gap comes amid concerns about the French government's ability to implement budget cuts, while German debt is perceived as a safe haven.

data.title: Former Eli Lilly Exec Sells Wyoming Estate for Close to $39.5 Million — WSJ
data.description:
By E.B. Solomont

A former executive at Eli Lilly-maker of popular weight-loss drug Zepbound-has sold a roughly 117-acre estate in the Jackson Hole, Wyo., area for close to its asking price of $39.5 million in one of the valley's highest sales.

Dr. Jan Lundberg and his wife, Ingeborg Lundberg, who live primarily in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., listed the property last year. Jan said the couple sold because they are purchasing a home in Sweden, where he is doing more board and venture-capital work.

Jan was president of Lilly Research Laboratories from 2010 to 2018. He was previously a research executive at pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca. Jan said his family benefited from the success of Eli Lilly's GLP-1 pipeline, which grew during his tenure.

"One of the reasons why we could afford to buy such a home in Jackson Hole was the advances of the Lilly portfolio and the shares I got from the company with time," Jan said.

The Lundbergs purchased the Jackson Hole property in 2021. It was last asking $33.9 million. Perched atop the East Gros Ventre Butte, the estate has multiple residences, including a mountain-style main house with log, stone and glass finishes.

Built in 2009, the roughly 12,700-square-foot main house has five bedrooms and an indoor pool. The property also has three ponds and a creek.

Listing agent Latham Jenkins of Live Water Properties said the property's roughly 18,000 square feet of living space is far more than is currently permissible to build in Jackson Hole, where zoning rules limit the size of new houses being built.

"A property today can't be more than 10,000 square feet," Jenkins said. Roughly 70% of the property's acreage is held in a conservation easement and cannot be developed.

The Lundbergs previously had a Big Sky, Mont., property in the upscale Yellowstone Club, where "Shark Tank" investor Robert Herjavec and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg have owned homes. The elevation, however, was too high, so they sold it for a $10 million profit, which they used to buy the Jackson Hole home, Jan said.

Jackson Hole is a magnet for uber-wealthy buyers. The town of Jackson's median single-family home price was $2.75 million for the three months ending Aug. 31, up 21.5% year-over-year, according to real-estate brokerage Redfin.

Jenkins said the $20 million-plus sector is particularly active. "People buy here as a safe haven and a tax haven," he said. In June, the actor, filmmaker and studio head Tyler Perry listed his estate in Jackson for $39.5 million. The priciest home sold in Jackson is a 55-acre estate that traded in 2021, according to Jenkins. It was last listed for $65 million.

Morgan Bruemmer of the Clear Creek Group represented the buyer. Bruemmer declined to identify his client, but said the property wasn't the buyer's first home in Jackson and that the buyer was "looking for a larger piece of property."

data.title: Why bond investors quickly lost their enthusiasm for weak jobs figures
data.description:
By Isabel Wang and Christine Idzelis

A weak jobs report briefly saw U.S. debt rally, but yields climbed back as investors worried inflation could stay hot if the Fed hikes less

Bad news finally worked in Treasurys' favor - but just for a little while.

A weak U.S. jobs report did what bad news hadn't done in a while: It made U.S. debt look like a safe haven again - albeit briefly.

U.S. Treasurys gave up an early rally on Friday after a weaker-than-expected jobs report initially sent investors rushing into government debt.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note BX:TMUBMUSD10Y fell 8 basis points to 5.155%, before reversing the move by midday trading. The policy-sensitive 2-year yield BX:TMUBMUSD02Y erased an 8.4-basis-point drop and turned sharply higher to 4.820%, according to FactSet data. Bond yields and prices move in the opposite direction to each other.

Data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September, which was well below expectations. The unemployment rate also ticked higher to 4.2%.

"Friday's cool jobs report doesn't guarantee lower yields, because the underlying drivers - inflation and sky-high government debt - are not going anywhere," said Nic Puckrin, macro and cross-asset analyst and founder of the Coin Bureau. "That means Americans must prepare for the double whammy of higher unemployment and rising prices at the store and at the pump, right in time for the winter holidays."

Treasury yields had a "knee-jerk" reaction lower after Friday's employment report showed the pace of jobs growth was cooler than economists expected.

Still, the economy is doing "fine," Chris Galipeau, head market strategist at the Franklin Templeton Institute, told MarketWatch. His view is that the 10-year yield's recent climb above 5% comes from "real economic growth," rather than long-term inflation fears.

To be sure, the weaker-than-expected jobs report wasn't the only force at work to push Treasury yields sharply lower early Friday. Yields surged in the third quarter, and some investors considered Treasurys to be oversold heading into Friday's session. Portfolio rebalancing at the start of the new quarter may have steered some capital back into beaten-down Treasurys, helping fixed income catch a brief bid.

Yet the jobs report didn't change the big-picture issues facing the Federal Reserve: Inflation remains a concern, the energy shock from the Iran war still is playing out globally, and traders still expect more interest-rate hikes from the central bank.

Fed-funds futures on Friday suggested an October hike looks unlikely. However, there was almost an 87% chance that the Fed would raise its benchmark rate in December by at least a quarter of a percentage point, from its current target range of 3.75% to 4%, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

"The data helped ease a bit of the pressure on the Fed to keep a hiking cycle in place, and now we can sit back and let the market determine risk on its own without the Fed having to get involved in setting the overnight rate higher for the time being," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management.

That also explains why stocks were holding their ground despite the leg higher in Treasury yields, Mulberry told MarketWatch via phone on Friday.

"Equities can go higher while the 10-year Treasury goes higher because the fundamentals of the economy are still reasonably strong," he said.

The uptick in Treasury yields also came as oil prices (CL00) (BRN00) bounced from their session lows, erasing most of their earlier losses and underscoring how quickly inflation concerns can resurface.

U.S. stocks were higher Friday afternoon, with the Nasdaq Composite COMP up 1.2%, the S&P 500 SPX up 0.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA 0.4% higher, according to FactSet data.

-Isabel Wang -Christine Idzelis

data.title: US FDA closes lettuce parasite probe, links outbreak to Mexico facility
data.description:
The US FDA said on Friday it has concluded its investigation into a summer parasite outbreak, linking the illnesses to recalled shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico.

While investigators could not definitively determine how the contamination happened, tests confirmed the Cyclospora parasite was present in the environment where the lettuce was grown and processed, the health regulator said.

Patient illness reports and supply-chain tracking strongly supported the link between the recalled lettuce and the multistate outbreak, which causes intestinal sickness, it said.

After the probe concluded, the US Food and Drug Administration announced a 10-point plan to prevent similar outbreaks ahead of the 2027 growing season.
